_schema_notes.purpose: Structural template for extracting DRHP data into a queryable, citation-grounded knowledge base. Python populates this from the PDF. The LLM only reads it — it never re-derives a fact that isn't already computed here.
_schema_notes.disclosure_status_rule: DRAFT RHPs contain '[●]' placeholders for figures not yet finalized (price band, lot size, post-Offer allocation). These MUST be stored as disclosure_status='PENDING_DISCLOSURE', value=null. Never estimate, infer, or silently omit a pending field. The LLM must state 'not yet disclosed in this draft' rather than guessing or staying silent.

category_tag_enum.1_direct_lookup: Fact copied verbatim from a KB node, cited with source_page.
category_tag_enum.2_derived_inference: Computed in Python by walking an ALLOWED relationship in inference_rules.json. Must show which KB fields were combined.
category_tag_enum.3_out_of_scope: Not answerable from this KB. Must trigger refusal per inference_rules.json blocklist.

use_of_proceeds.unit: structured: gross/net proceeds + objects list with amounts
use_of_proceeds.note: Amounts often disclosed before percentages/net figure — expect PARTIAL disclosure_status until Offer Price is finalized.

industry_market_size.note: Quote DRHP's own commissioned industry report figure. Never project forward.

L1b_management_continuity.note: Raw tenure facts only. 'Stability' is a judgment word — never stored or asserted here.

L2_financial_core.note: Populated per Fiscal Year. All ratios/growth figures computed in Python, never by the LLM.

L3_valuation.note: Only populated if DRHP itself discloses a peer comparison table. No externally sourced peers.

promoter_holding.materiality_note: Board-defined materiality thresholds go here verbatim — these become hardcoded Python inclusion rules, not LLM judgment calls.

glossary.note: Reference-only. LLM may quote a definition verbatim with citation but must never reason over glossary terms to derive an analytical claim. Terms defined BY THE RHP ITSELF only — requires source_page. For general financial/accounting jargon the RHP does not define, see financial_ontology instead.

financial_ontology.note: General financial/accounting term definitions (RoNW, EPS, P/E, D/E, CAGR, materiality, etc.) — standard knowledge, NOT specific to or disclosed by any particular RHP. No source_page field — these are not document citations. Distinct from glossary, which holds only RHP-defined terms. Narration must frame these as general knowledge, never as something 'the RHP says'.
